observedFailure.observedError: local-resume/database/LOCK already locked by another process
observedFailure.enteredBoundary: Local-resume predecessor finished done with no error and checkpoint list succeeded; durable readback then failed before current runtime resume.

changedBehavior: The parent fixture no longer opens embedded KV; each durable phase runs in an owned child of the existing integration executable and shares one public production SurrealDbProvider for protected envelope, raw checkpoint, epoch and claim readback.
Source/corruption phases and final/no-claims phases reuse that single provider; corruption still mutates the real durable source through the public production client.
The parent joins child OS exit before another readback or production runtime can acquire the same KV. An owned Child guard kills/reaps it if the fixture unwinds.
The unchanged full integration entrypoint dispatches its private readback-job child mode. No test filter, independent gate, unit/mock proof, or extra production authority path was introduced.

All production JWT/API/restart/race/kill/unsupported assertions remain in the parent whole target. Database provider strings serialize identically; internal fixture ownership uses an owned String for private job serialization.

causeAssessment.evidence: The scenario called envelopes(Database.connect), immediately proof(Database.connect), then started the next runtime. The corruption scenario also opened separate providers for inspection and mutation. Both helper scopes lacked a joined close boundary. The shared connect panic cannot establish which opening failed or which process held the lock.

guards.name: single_provider_per_durable_phase
guards.trace: Observed lock conflict on sequential embedded provider openings; envelope/proof/mutation assertions now share one provider.

guards.name: joined_readback_process_before_next_kv_owner
guards.trace: Observed local exclusive store conflict; OS child exit is joined before any next owner, without retry/sleep-based lock admission.

guards.name: owned_readback_child_cleanup
guards.trace: The new process holds an exclusive store; fixture unwind must kill/reap that exact owned child.

privateChildContract.environment: UAR_DOT06_READBACK_JOB=<0600 private job file> on the child only
privateChildContract.providerPath: Public production SurrealDbProvider/PersistenceLayer/client APIs; no crate-private adapter.
privateChildContract.processRole: durable-readback; executable is the integration test image, not the production server
privateChildContract.samplingInstruction: Use readback-process.json to retain exact child PID/join/exit. Distinguish its test-image binding from production runtime process.json. Child test output is private and never counts as an accepted scenario group.

verification.reason: Root authorized complete fixture correction only; no check/gate runs before root review and explicit whole-target GO.

nextGate.environment: Fresh root-owned namespace/evidence directory and qualified private infrastructure; outer gate has no UAR_DOT06_READBACK_JOB.
nextGate.streams: Held until root authorizes after resume acceptance.

risks: Correction compilation and runtime behavior remain unverified until the full gate.
The entrypoint has a private fixture-child mode; outer acceptance must remain environment-cleared and require the complete 24-group inventory. Private child completion is not full-slice acceptance.
Acceptance sampling must classify readback test-image children separately from production server processes; their exact join records remain private.
At-failure lock holder and the failing connect were not observed, so no predecessor-retained-lock assertion is made.
preserved: 21-source binding; only the two approved fixture files changed
